candidate_requirements.requirement: Request quantitative oral and intravenous intake and net fluid balance for cycle 2 days 0–4
candidate_requirements.rationale: Distinguishing polyuric hyponatremia mechanisms (water overload vs renal salt/water loss) is impossible without intake and balance data
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: 24-hour intake records, fluid charts, or documented net balance
candidate_requirements.deadline: Proposed request at the current day-4 assessment

candidate_requirements.requirement: Request objective volume-status findings (examination, weights, vitals, orthostatics)
candidate_requirements.rationale: Extracellular volume status discriminates hypovolemic (cisplatin nephrotoxicity/salt wasting) from euvolemic (SIADH/water intoxication) hyponatremia
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Documented exam, daily weights, or hemodynamic data
candidate_requirements.deadline: Proposed request at the current day-4 assessment

candidate_requirements.requirement: Request desmopressin dose, route and administration timing relative to the polyuria, and any recent changes
candidate_requirements.rationale: A 9.75 L/day urine output in known central DI strongly suggests desmopressin underdosing, missed doses, or malabsorption, which is directly actionable
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Medication administration record review or patient/caregiver report
candidate_requirements.deadline: Proposed request at the current day-4 assessment

candidate_requirements.requirement: Request sampling times of sodium/urine values and any additional serial sodium measurements with hydrocortisone administration timing
candidate_requirements.rationale: Timing relative to fluids and stress-dose steroids affects interpretation; adrenal insufficiency can cause both hyponatremia and impaired water excretion
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Documented lab timestamps or repeat sodium panel
candidate_requirements.deadline: Proposed request at the current day-4 assessment
